experiment: Structural search Phase 1, family (a): on rung 2 resume-projection-integrity and rung 4 pure-result-replay, do the five authored catalog seeds and the accepted unguided I1 children of direct differ in blind judge quality by more than two pooled within-arm standard deviations on both tasks, with DIRECT not the sole winner and I1 not collapsed?
solutions: not recorded here: this file sits in the runtime agents can read; the operator passes each task's solution commit with --solution and the scan uses it
arms: one per evaluation: each evaluation runs through prepare.run_arm with its evaluation id as the arm, so summarize reports one arm per evaluation; evaluation ids depend on the environment manifest and are not known before the runs, so none is listed. Policies are joined to evaluations by scoring.join_scores through each run row's records directory

policies.unguided: unguided:<candidate_id> per accepted I1 child of direct, reported descriptively; all children's evaluations of a task are also pooled as one arm named unguided

batches: one pool per task (scoring.pool_evaluations): the final patch of every completed, uncontaminated evaluation of that task, shuffled, stable-sorted by policy and dealt round-robin into the fewest batches of at most ten clones (at most eight evaluations, sizes differing by at most one, a policy's replicates in different batches when there are several) with both anchors repeated in every batch (harness D4 batch size)
scale: each clone scores 0-8, the sum of score.orc's four rubric criteria (root_cause, scope, generality, layering), each 0-2, averaged over the judges not excluded; an evaluation's value is its final clone's (summarize's run value)
primary_measure: the blind rubric mean per task and arm: the mean of summarize's run values over the arm's valued evaluations, computed by scoring.phase1_readout from results.json joined by scoring.join_scores; arms are the catalog policies and the pooled unguided arm
primary_note: empty: summarize measures are per arm, here per evaluation, so no summarize measure names a policy; summarize reads only judges, primary and secondary from a criterion and accepts empty lists. The primary measure and the rules below are applied by scoring.phase1_readout

separation.arms: catalog policies and the pooled unguided arm with two or more valued evaluations on the task; a single child is reported only
separation.rule: a task is separated when the largest difference between two compared arms' means exceeds the threshold max(tolerance_sd times the pooled within-arm SD, min_tolerance rubric points) and its anchor spread is within anchor_spread_limit for every judge; the pooled SD is sqrt(sum((n-1) s^2) / sum(n-1)) over the compared arms; with none it is unavailable and the task is not separated

direct_sole_winner: on a task, DIRECT is a compared arm and its mean exceeds every other compared arm's mean by more than the separation threshold; DIRECT's rank is its competition rank among compared arms
decision: first rule that fires: any pool with anchors_ok false -> anchors_inverted; fewer than min_tasks separated tasks -> within_tolerance; DIRECT the sole winner on every separated task -> direct_sole_winner; the I1 collapse figure unavailable (no accepted child: the adaptive claim is untested) -> collapse_unavailable; I1 collapsed -> collapsed; otherwise separated and phase2_selected is true. Phase 2 needs trusted anchors, separation on at least min_tasks tasks and an available collapse figure at or below the threshold for at least one interface; I1 is the only Phase 1 interface
reported: per task: catalog policy, child and pooled unguided runs, mean, within-arm SD, hidden_mean, calls_mean, wall_clock_mean
per task: compared arms, pooled SD, threshold, largest gap, separated, DIRECT's rank, anchors_ok, anchor_spread per judge, judge agreement, excluded judges, unpooled completed evaluations
unguided I1: episode outcomes, distinct skeletons, revisit rate, terminal-only share, allocation_distinct, collapsed
anchor scores per batch and judge (summarize results.json)
hidden_acceptance: descriptive only: reported per policy, never a threshold, gate, rank or selection
known_differences: with more than eight evaluations of a task, policies are rated in different batches; anchors are repeated in each batch and their scores reported per batch and judge
model_policy: no call uses a Fable model (owner, 2026-10-15): arms, mutators, judges and in-process subagents run behind the shims' model guard
anchor_trust: from each pool's results.json anchors: anchors_ok when, in every batch and for every judge not excluded, the upstream anchor's total is strictly above the stub's (a missing anchor fails); anchor_spread per judge is the largest difference of one anchor's total across batches. Each pool's results.json criterion_sha256 must equal this file's SHA-256
collapse: collapsed when the driver readout's terminal_only_share exceeds collapse_threshold; terminal_only_share is the roadmap's collapse share: the share of accepted children whose skeleton and provider allocation both equal the parent's (children with the parent's skeleton but another allocation count as allocation_distinct, not as collapsed); unavailable without an accepted child
